title: Quotes: ' and "
summary: Single quotes keep text as it is, double quotes still expand $: when to use which.

text: - Single quotes: everything stays exactly as written.
- Double quotes: $variables and $( ) are still replaced.

scheme: rm $file       rm gets: my │ notes.txt  2 files!
rm "$file"     rm gets: my notes.txt     1 file
text: Without quotes, the shell cuts the value at each space.
- Always write "$file" with double quotes: it stays one argument.
- In scripts this one habit prevents many bugs.
Use single quotes when a program has its own special characters.
- The shell leaves them alone and the program gets them as they are.
